rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a single ALD Pt coating on ceria, whereas the target used a closed-loop high-throughput campaign iterating composition and synthesis parameters across 5–19 element alloys on La-doped alumina. These are fundamentally different kinds of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses 700 °C aging in oxidizing/humid atmosphere, while the target used 900 °C cyclic lean/rich aging with a specific multicomponent feed and light-off testing from 100–500 °C. The regimes differ substantially in temperature, atmosphere, and test protocol.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced sintering and improved oxygen activation via metal–support interaction, whereas the target mechanism involves electronic redistribution, Cu–Pt cooperative sites, and redox coupling between hydrocarbon oxidation and NO reduction. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher reaction rates and lower deactivation with ~30% less Pt, while the target predicted and found more catalysts surpassing Pd in low-temperature and total conversion after severe aging. The property (activity/durability) and direction (improvement) align only in a general sense.
